sections.html:
Virginia's far western edge is where Alleghany County lies, in the top corner of the Roanoke Region. The Allegheny Mountains form its western flank and lend the county its name. Formed on January 5, 1822, from parts of Bath, Botetourt and Monroe counties, it spans 449.7 square miles, about 0.7 percent of them water, and held 15,223 people in 2020. Neighbors are Bath, Rockbridge, Botetourt and Craig counties, plus Monroe and Greenbrier in West Virginia. Near Iron Gate, the Cowpasture and Jackson Rivers meet just beyond the boundary and become the James.

Covington serves as county seat but is an independent city outside the county, so a Covington address may be billed by the city instead of Alleghany County. Look at the bill itself to see which office issued it. Clifton Forge is the biggest town within the county and regained town status on July 1, 2001, with Iron Gate and Low Moor the other places people name most.

Work here depends on a few large employers, such as a paperboard mill in Covington and a rail fueling yard in Clifton Forge, and many residents drive to Lewisburg, Lexington or Roanoke. That keeps the local buyer pool small. Cash buyers can take a house exactly as it stands, which suits owners who would rather not wait on a financed buyer.

Interstate 64 runs east and west through the county, and U.S. Route 220 runs north and south. Amtrak's Cardinal stops at Clifton Forge, about 12 miles from Covington. With so many residents commuting, buyers weigh interstate access heavily, so spell out your own road access when you speak to one.

Virginia splits the work: the commissioner of the revenue supervises assessment, and the treasurer collects. A locality may reassess every one to six years. Values are normally fixed as of January 1, and an owner who disagrees can appeal to the local board of equalization.

The county complex is at 9212 Winterberry Avenue in Covington. Ask the treasurer and the commissioner of the revenue for your current bill, its due date and the amount you will owe through your closing date.

sections.h2: How the Board of Equalization works
sections.html:
This board listens to assessment complaints and may raise, lower or keep an assessment. You can reach it in three ways:

  • Call (540) 863-6640 on a weekday between 8 am and 5 pm, holidays excluded, and book a 15 minute slot.
  • Mail a written complaint to 9212 Winterberry Avenue, Suite E, Covington, VA 24426.
  • Show up at a hearing and speak or hand in written material.

The law assumes the assessment is correct, so the burden is yours. You win by showing it is not uniform with similar properties, backed by substantial evidence, or that it exceeds fair market value. Hearing dates differ from year to year, so ask the county which schedule goes with your notice.

Your last avenue is the circuit court. Section 58.1-3984 of the Virginia Code allows an aggrieved owner to apply there. The deadline is whichever comes later: three years after the tax year ends, or one year after the assessment date, and the statute lists a few other situations.

Courts start from the assessor's figure, or the board's figure if it changed the value, and you carry the burden of proving otherwise by a preponderance of the evidence. A lawsuit rarely makes sense when you are about to sell, since the contract price is what establishes the value.

sections.h2: Back taxes and the closing table
sections.html:
A tax lien stays on the parcel until the taxing authority is paid, and under section 58.1-3340 it outranks other liens on real estate. So if you sell with a bill outstanding, the buyer's money pays it before you see anything. The purchase agreement should say who covers the current year's share. Your title company or settlement attorney will normally call the treasurer for a payoff figure ahead of closing.

  • Request the balance through the date you expect to close.
  • If two or more years are open, start with the oldest bill.
  • Keep the receipt in case the title company asks for it.

Three jurisdictions can touch an address here: the county, the independent city of Covington, and the town of Clifton Forge. A house inside Covington is handled by the city, not the county. Look at the name and return address on your last bill. If you are unsure, call the county treasurer before you list, so the payoff comes from the right place.

The same check helps your buyer. A lender and a title company will ask which locality issued the bill, and a quick, correct answer keeps closing on schedule. It also tells you which board of equalization to contact if you want to contest a value before you sell, and whether the county's Winterberry Avenue complex or another office is the right door.

The General Assembly sets a ceiling and each locality adopts its own terms by ordinance, so the local figure can sit below it. For the full recording cost, including local charges, ask the circuit court clerk.

ChargeVirginia rule
Late penalty (section 58.1-3916)Up to 10 percent of the overdue tax, or $10 if that is more
Interest (section 58.1-3916)Up to 10 percent a year
Grantor tax (section 58.1-802)50 cents per $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise
State recordation tax (section 58.1-801)25 cents per $100

sections.h2: A short checklist before you list
sections.html:
• Find the last tax bill and note the name of the office that mailed it.
  • Phone (540) 863-6640 if the assessment looks high compared with similar houses nearby, and ask how to reach the board.
  • Ask the treasurer for a balance through the day you hope to close.
  • Write down your road access, since I-64 and U.S. 220 are what commuters ask about.
  • Decide whether you want to repair first, list as-is, or take a cash offer.

Having these five items settled before the first buyer call makes the first calls with a buyer or title company much simpler.

sections.h2: What Alleghany County sellers often face
sections.html:
A few problems come up again and again for owners here.

  • Tax that fell behind on a house that sits empty.
  • Repairs the owner cannot afford before listing.
  • A small pool of local buyers.
  • Doubt about whether the county or the city of Covington bills the address.

If one of these is yours, we will look at the house as it is and send a written cash offer, and you pay for no repairs. Call or text the address. Before you do, locate the latest tax bill and any notice from the commissioner of the revenue, so the first conversation can cover real numbers. We can ask the treasurer for the payoff and build the closing around it, and any balance is paid from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Is Covington part of Alleghany County?
faqs.a: No. It is the county seat, yet it is an independent city, and houses inside its limits are handled by the city. Your bill shows which office sent it.

faqs.q: What is the largest town in Alleghany County?
faqs.a: Clifton Forge. It reincorporated as a town within the county on July 1, 2001.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Alleghany County assessment?
faqs.a: Go to the county Board of Equalization. Phone (540) 863-6640 to book a time, or mail a written complaint to 9212 Winterberry Avenue, Suite E, Covington. Your case has to show the value exceeds market or is out of line with similar properties.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over a house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the tax is settled at closing. The lien outranks other liens, so the balance usually comes out of the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the most a Virginia locality can charge for a late real estate tax payment?
faqs.a: The penalty ceiling is 10 percent of the overdue tax or $10, whichever is more, and interest tops out at 10 percent a year. Each local ordinance sets the real terms.
